title: Basic automation patterns
summary: Copyable patterns for buttons, relays, timers, MQTT, displays, battery, and audio.
body:
Button toggles relay

Physical Button Rising Edge → Relay Toggle In

Both adapters are supported. Verify switch polarity and relay active level with the load disconnected.

Delayed relay

Button Rising Edge → Relay ON
Button Rising Edge → Delay 10 s → Relay OFF

The two paths start together. A second trigger creates the behavior documented for the selected timing block; test retrigger expectations.

Cyclic telemetry

On Start → Timer 30 s → MQTT Publish In
Battery Voltage → Append value

Use Timer, not Delay, for periodic execution.

Low battery warning

Battery Low → Rising Edge → MQTT Publish
Battery Low → Rising Edge → Audio Play

Rising Edge sends once when the condition becomes true; Cooldown can rate-limit a different repeatedly-triggered alarm.

Display a message

Button Rising Edge → I2C OLED Set text In
Text “System enabled” → Set text Text

Only the primary I2C OLED profile currently has Set text/Clear runtime support.

Not yet runtime-supported

The LED PWM dimmer, generic fan/MOSFET/pump profiles, most environmental sensors, and arbitrary analog level sensors have configuration profiles but no generic firmware Logics adapter. Do not present them as executable recipes until adapters are added.

title: Lighting, gate, alarm, and multi-sensor designs
summary: Build larger systems from the runtime capabilities that exist today.
body:
Motion-triggered relay light

PIR Rising Edge → Relay ON
PIR Falling Edge → Delay 60 s → Relay OFF

PIR and relay runtime adapters are supported. A light sensor profile/driver is not currently available, so dusk qualification is a future enhancement unless a supported analog input is deliberately adapted and calibrated.

Gate or valve actuator

Use the dedicated DRV8833 Motor page and end switches. Assign Opening/Closing roles, a maximum duration, and a corresponding limit input. MQTT open/close/switch commands are implemented. PWM speed is not.

Door alarm

Reed Switch Rising Edge → MQTT Publish “Door opened”
Reed Switch Falling Edge → MQTT Publish “Door closed”

Match edge direction to wiring polarity. Use an independent subscriber for phone notifications.

Multiple sensors and relays

Each configured slot receives a stable identity. Use descriptive physical names and separate automation groups. Current firmware adapters cover a narrower set than the palette: verify each peripheral page before designing the graph.

Greenhouse and irrigation reality check

A full humidity, soil-moisture, fan, valve, and pump controller is a useful target, but several relevant profiles are currently wiring-only. A source-backed partial design can use supported relay outputs, reed/float switches, battery monitoring, MQTT, and DRV8833 motion. Environmental and soil sensors require implemented adapters before the complete project is supported.

title: Practical project FAQ
summary: Direct answers to common ELMA-IoT design questions.
body:
How do I stop a relay chattering near a threshold?

Use separate ON and OFF thresholds, such as ON above 30 °C and OFF below 27 °C. Debounce is for rapid triggers, not measurement hysteresis.

How do I send every five seconds?

Use Timer set to 5 seconds feeding the action Flow input. Connect the live value separately to its data input. Delay alone fires only after an incoming trigger.

How do I get a phone notification?

Publish an MQTT event. Home Assistant or another subscriber generates the phone notification; ELMA-IoT does not directly push one.

Can I use DRV8833 speed control?

Direction, duration, limits, and MQTT movement commands are implemented. PWM speed is not currently supported by the dedicated runtime.

Can I use any profile shown in Configuration?

No. Some profiles provide wiring and pin validation only. Read the Runtime support banner on the peripheral page.

What happens if a sensor disappears?

Where the adapter exposes Available/Error, build an explicit safe action and alarm path. ELMA-IoT cannot infer the safe physical state.

Can I build a true key-to-frequency piano?

Recorded Piano melody blocks and button-triggered melodies are supported. A general arbitrary frequency API is not currently supported.
